**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity) on § 10 NONASSIGNABILITY (p0042).**

What I found:
- **Assignment (§ 10, p0042)** is the only relevant provision. It is mutual and uses a reasonable-consent standard — but it requires the other party's consent for *every* transfer, with no carve-out for assignment to a Company affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets. That misses the fallback position (right to assign to successors), so it is a material deviation rather than an acceptable fallback.
- **Change of control:** no "change of control" or "deemed an assignment" language exists anywhere in the document. § 6 termination is limited to convenience when no SOW is outstanding and uncured material breach (p0032–p0033), so RadialSpark gets no exit or re-pricing right on our change of control. No walk-away trigger.

Redline (validated, `ok:true`): appended to § 10 — "*; provided that Company may assign this Agreement without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets*," tracking the approved `seed-assign` precedent.

Noted in the rationale rather than redlined: we did not add the preferred-position bar on Contractor assigning to a Clear Capital competitor, as that is a refinement beyond the material terms.
